11	/-!
12	# The DD-R carve locus `Z(♦)` over the pair charts (DDR-1)
13	
14	The carve locus of the DAT-D design (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1;
15	`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §3.1): over each pair chart `Spec (R^I ⊗[k] R^J)` of the
16	Grassmannian pair, the tautological pair `(K_taut^I, K_taut^J)` is carved by the SINGLE
17	closed condition `(♦)` — for every multiplier the carve-pair arrow
18	`K_taut^I → (H₂ ⊗ R_{I,J}) ⧸ K_taut^J` vanishes — cut out by the carve ideal `I_♦`
19	(the span of the `entriesIdeal`s of the carve arrows).
20	
21	Following the spec §3 preamble, the scheme side is developed for the coordinate ambients
22	`H = Fin r → k`; the abstract window spaces `H_M`, `H_{M+s}` enter through the DD-4
23	boundary bases (`Module.finBasis` at the consumer seam), which conjugate the section
24	multiplication `sectionMulBilin` into the coordinate multiplier family `divCarveMul`.
25	The generic layer (`carveIdeal`, `carveLocus`, keystones, the gluing compatibility) is
26	stated for an arbitrary multiplier family and instantiated by the campaign spellings
27	(`divCarveArrow`, `divCarveIdeal`, `divCarveLocus`).
28	
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pairTautFst/Snd`: the tautological Grassmannian pair over a pair
30	  chart ring.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdeal`: the carve ideal `I_♦` of a multiplier family.
32	* **Keystones** (`carveIdeal_le_ker_iff`, `carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map`,
33	  `carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_factors`): a test map kills `I_♦` iff the base-changed carve
34	  arrows vanish (`(♦) ⊗ S` holds, via `carveArrow_baseChange_eq_zero_iff`'s
35	  `entriesIdeal` mechanism) iff the carve holds for the pulled-back Grassmannian pair
36	  (the carve transport L1) iff the map factors through the locus.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveLocus`, `carveLocusι`, `carveLocusToGrPair`: the chart-wise
38	  `Z(♦)` as a closed subscheme of the pair chart, mapped into `grPair`.
39	* **The gluing compatibility** (`carveIdeal_le_ker_of_specMap_pairChartMap_eq`): the
40	  carve ideals of two pair charts presenting a common test morphism to `grPair` have the
41	  same kill-sets — the mathematical content of "`Z(♦)` glues", via L1 + the GL-cocycle
42	  pair-chart compatibility.
43	* **Campaign spellings**: `divCarveMul`, `divCarveArrow`, `divCarveIdeal`,
44	  `divCarveLocus` at the windows `A = s·F`, `B = M·F` (through their `H⁰`-bases).
45	-/

64	the pullback of the chart-`I` tautological point along the left inclusion
65	`R^I → R^I ⊗ R^J`.  The `K_taut^I` of the carve. -/
66	noncomputable def pairTautFst (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
67	    grFunctorAff k (Fin r₁ → k) g (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) :=

73	The `K_taut^J` of the carve. -/
74	noncomputable def pairTautSnd (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :

76	  Module.Grassmannian.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
77	    (R := k) (A := ChartRing k g r₁ i.down.1))
78	    (chartTautologicalPoint k g r₂ j.down.1 j.down.2)

91	
92	variable {ι : Type u} (μ : ι → ((Fin r₁ → k) →ₗ[k] (Fin r₂ → k)))
93	
94	/-- **The carve ideal `I_♦`** of a multiplier family over a pair chart: the span of the
95	entries ideals of the carve-pair arrows of the tautological pair, over all multipliers.
96	Its vanishing locus is the chart-wise `Z(♦)`. -/
97	noncomputable def carveIdeal (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
98	    Ideal (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) :=
99	  ⨆ m : ι, entriesIdeal (carvePairArrow (μ m) (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule
100	    (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule)
101	
102	/-- **Keystone, base-change form**: a test algebra kills the carve ideal iff all the
103	base-changed carve arrows vanish — the `(♦) ⊗ S` condition, through the `entriesIdeal`
104	universal property (`carveArrow_baseChange_eq_zero_iff`'s mechanism). -/
105	theorem carveIdeal_le_ker_iff (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
106	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S] :
107	    carveIdeal k g r₁ r₂ μ i j
108	        ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S) ↔
109	      ∀ m, LinearMap.baseChange S (carvePairArrow (μ m)
110	        (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule
111	        (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule) = 0 := by
112	  rw [carveIdeal, iSup_le_iff]
113	  exact forall_congr' fun m => (baseChange_eq_zero_iff _ S).symm
114	
115	/-- **Keystone, pulled-back-pair form**: a test algebra kills the carve ideal iff the
116	carve holds for the pulled-back tautological pair over `S` (mathlib's
117	`Module.Grassmannian.map`, as `ker (baseChangeMkQ)`) — the carve transport L1. -/
118	theorem carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
119	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
120	    [Algebra (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S]
121	    [IsScalarTower k (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S] :
122	    carveIdeal k g r₁ r₂ μ i j
123	        ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S) ↔
124	      ∀ m, carvePairArrow (μ m)
125	        (LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ S

10	/-!
11	# Zariski-local certification of a seed system: relaxing the global certificate gate
12	
13	The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),
14	whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`
15	carries certified families over the localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` which are
16	divisor-equal to the pulled system.  **Nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a
17	certificate over `R` itself.**
18	
19	The certificate-assembly lane has nevertheless been attacking the *global* clause
20	`(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` over the chart ring `R_Z`, whose no-leak input
21	is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
22	whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
23	finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
24	its consumer needs.
25	
26	This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
27	certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
28	span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
29	pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`
30	specializes it to a seed: if the seed's adaptation acquires a certificate **after
31	localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support
32	tube produces (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`: piece isolation is available
33	Zariski-locally on the base, never globally) — then the seed's own system is locally
34	certified, and hence has a `DivFamZar` class.
35	
36	The mathematical content is the observation that `IsLocallyCertified` is designed to be
37	produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is
38	`DivEq` to the pulled adaptation's system on the nose; the localization step that makes
39	no-leak true is licensed here rather than being an unrecoverable obstruction.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — the span-`⊤` production
44	  rule for `IsLocallyCertified`, stated with `Localization.Away` charts.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_certified` —
46	  the seed form: away-local certificates give a locally certified seed system.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified` — the
48	  resulting `DivFamZar` class, the object every DD-R consumer actually wants.
49	-/

13	is `Spec` of the **carve chart ring** `R_Z = R_{I,J} ⧸ I_♦`, and the tautological pair
14	pushes to a universal Grassmannian pair over it which satisfies the carve after *every*
15	base change — in particular in every residue-field fibre, which is exactly where P-fib
16	(`RiemannRoch/PFib.lean`) takes over.

/-!
# The ε-pair and its pair-chart framing are CARRIER-INDIFFERENT

The DD-R representability consumer asks for the chart-typed value: `divRepClassifyZar`
(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) and `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange`
(`Picard/DivRepChartRange.lean`) both quantify over `DivFamZar`, and the chart data they need
comes from `DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean`).  Since the
widened comparison `DivFamZar.toAff` runs chart-typed → widened and has no reverse (a widened
cover has no chart typing to recover, and manufacturing one is the fixed-pair confinement that
protection I-0492 clause 3 forbids), it is natural to read this as "R2 has not reached the
consumer".

**That reading is wrong, and this file measures why.**  The chart dependency of
`exists_certChartCover` does not run through the divisor's *cover* at all.  It runs through the
**window**:

* `divFamEps` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`) is `divisorWindow G.eqns` at two windows, and
  `eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations` is a field of `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` exactly as it
  is of `CertifiedDivisorFamily`.  The cover never enters.
* the framing clause is two equations between submodules of `R ⊗[k] H`, comparing
  `Module.Grassmannian.map w` of a tautological subbundle against the base change of the window.
  Neither side mentions a cover, a piece, or a chart typing of the divisor.

So "which carrier the certificate lives on" and "where the ε-pair sits in the Grassmannian" are
independent questions, and the widening is invisible to the second.  The declarations below say
that in Lean rather than in prose: both are *statements* about a widened family, and their
elaboration is the content.

## What this does NOT claim

It does not prove `exists_certChartCover` over the widened carrier — that theorem's proof runs
the certificate cover and the per-piece frame covers, which is real work and belongs to whoever
restates it.  What is established is that no *type* obstruction stands in the way: the clause is
expressible, so the remaining question is a proof, not a redesign.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.eps` — the ε-pair of a **widened** certified
  family, computed from its `eqns` alone.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.IsPairChartFramed` — the framing clause of
  `exists_certChartCover`, stated over the widened carrier.
-/

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

noncomputable def eps (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
    Submodule R (R ⊗[k]
        ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))

/-- **The pair-chart framing clause, over the WIDENED carrier.**  Exactly the two Grassmannian
equations of `DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover`, with `divFamEps (DivFam.mk G)` replaced by

That this elaborates is the point: the framing is a condition on where the ε-pair sits in the
Grassmannian, and the ε-pair does not know which cover certified the family.  So no *type*
obstruction separates the widened carrier from the chart-cover extraction the representability
consumer runs — see the module docstring for what is still owed. -/
def IsPairChartFramed (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g)
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
    (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →ₐ[k] R) : Prop :=
  (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange R b₁.equivFun.toLinearMap)
        (F.eps hpi g).1
    ∧ (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange R b₂.equivFun.toLinearMap)
        (F.eps hpi g).2

-- default recursion depth on the way

/-- The ε-pair of a widened family is its two windows, by definition.  Recorded because it is
the seam a restatement of `exists_certChartCover` would rewrite along. -/
@[simp]
lemma eps_fst (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
    (F.eps hpi g).1 = divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowM C pi hpi g) := rfl

-- as `eps_fst`
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
set_option maxRecDepth 4000 in
@[simp]
lemma eps_snd (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R g) :
    (F.eps hpi g).2 = divisorWindow F.eqns (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C pi hpi g) := rfl

/-! ## K1/K4: ambient coordinate transport and its naturality -/

section CongrAmbient

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {H H' : Type u} [AddCommGroup H] [Module k H] [AddCommGroup H'] [Module k H']
variable {g : ℕ} {T : Type u} [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]

/-- The quotient comparison of the ambient transport: quotients by a submodule and by
its image under the base-changed ambient equivalence agree. -/
noncomputable def congrAmbientQuotEquiv (e : H ≃ₗ[k] H') (x : grFunctorAff k H g T) :
    (TensorProduct k T H ⧸ x.toSubmodule) ≃ₗ[T]
      (TensorProduct k T H' ⧸
        Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T e.toLinearMap) x.toSubmodule) :=
  Submodule.Quotient.equiv x.toSubmodule _ (LinearEquiv.baseChange k T H H' e) rfl

/-- **K1 — ambient coordinate transport**: a `k`-linear identification of ambient
spaces carries Grassmannian points across, by `Submodule.map` of the base-changed
equivalence.  Packages the coordinate points `K^c` of the G-5 worksheet (§1.1): the
window points of `ε` read through the DD-4 boundary bases. -/
noncomputable def congrAmbient (e : H ≃ₗ[k] H') (x : grFunctorAff k H g T) :
    grFunctorAff k H' g T where
  toSubmodule := Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T e.toLinearMap) x.toSubmodule
  finite_quotient := Module.Finite.equiv (congrAmbientQuotEquiv e x)
  projective_quotient := Module.Projective.of_equiv (congrAmbientQuotEquiv e x)
  rankAtStalk_eq p := by
    rw [← congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv (congrAmbientQuotEquiv e x)) p]
    exact x.rankAtStalk_eq p

@[simp]
lemma congrAmbient_toSubmodule (e : H ≃ₗ[k] H') (x : grFunctorAff k H g T) :
    (congrAmbient e x).toSubmodule
      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T e.toLinearMap) x.toSubmodule :=
  rfl

/-- Freeness of the quotient transports across the ambient identification. -/
theorem free_quotient_congrAmbient (e : H ≃ₗ[k] H') (x : grFunctorAff k H g T)
    (hfree : Module.Free T (TensorProduct k T H ⧸ x.toSubmodule)) :
    Module.Free T (TensorProduct k T H' ⧸ (congrAmbient e x).toSubmodule) :=
  haveI := hfree
  Module.Free.of_equiv (congrAmbientQuotEquiv e x)

/-- `Submodule.baseChange` exchanges with `Submodule.map`: the base change of a mapped
submodule is the image of the base-changed submodule under the base-changed map. -/
theorem baseChange_map_submodule {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M M' : Type u}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (N : Submodule R M) :
    (Submodule.map f N).baseChange A
      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange A f) (N.baseChange A) := by
  have hcomp : f ∘ₗ N.subtype = (Submodule.map f N).subtype ∘ₗ f.submoduleMap N :=
    LinearMap.ext fun x => rfl
  have h1 : (Submodule.map f N).baseChange A
      = LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange A (Submodule.map f N).subtype) := rfl
  have h2 : N.baseChange A = LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange A N.subtype) := rfl
  rw [h1, h2, ← LinearMap.range_comp, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hcomp,
    LinearMap.baseChange_comp, LinearMap.range_comp,
    LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr (LinearMap.baseChange_surjective A
      (LinearMap.submoduleMap_surjective f N)), Submodule.map_top]

/-- **K4 — naturality of the ambient transport**: `congrAmbient` commutes with
mathlib's `Module.Grassmannian.map` along any `k`-algebra map.  Submodule content: the
`ker (baseChangeMkQ)` description of both sides (`ker_baseChangeMkQ_eq_map_baseChange`,
projective-quotient instances are the points' own) plus the `cancelBaseChange`
naturality square. -/
theorem map_congrAmbient {T' : Type u} [CommRing T'] [Algebra k T'] (α : T →ₐ[k] T')
    (e : H ≃ₗ[k] H') (x : grFunctorAff k H g T) :
    Module.Grassmannian.map α (congrAmbient e x)
      = congrAmbient e (Module.Grassmannian.map α x) := by
  letI : Algebra T T' := α.toAlgebra
  letI : IsScalarTower k T T' :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k T T')
  haveI hproj : Module.Projective T (TensorProduct k T H' ⧸
      Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T e.toLinearMap) x.toSubmodule) :=
    (congrAmbient e x).projective_quotient
  refine Module.Grassmannian.ext ?_
  have h1 := Module.Grassmannian.map_toSubmodule α (congrAmbient e x)
  have h2 := Module.Grassmannian.map_toSubmodule α x
  rw [h1, congrAmbient_toSubmodule, congrAmbient_toSubmodule, h2,
    Grassmannian.ker_baseChangeMkQ_eq_map_baseChange T'
      (Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T e.toLinearMap) x.toSubmodule),
    Grassmannian.ker_baseChangeMkQ_eq_map_baseChange T' x.toSubmodule,
    baseChange_map_submodule, ← Submodule.map_comp, ← Submodule.map_comp,
    cancelBaseChange_comp_baseChange_baseChange T' e.toLinearMap]

end CongrAmbient

theorem exists_matrixPoint_eq_of_free {T : Type u} [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]

    ∃ (X : Matrix (Fin g) (Fin r) T) (hX : Function.Surjective (matrixProj k g r T X)),

  have hcard : Fintype.card (Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex T
      (TensorProduct k T (Fin r → k) ⧸ x.toSubmodule)) = g := by
    rw [← Module.finrank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex]
    exact hfin

    (Module.Free.chooseBasis T _).reindex (Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard) with hb

    b.equivFun.toLinearMap ∘ₗ x.toSubmodule.mkQ with hφ
  set X : Matrix (Fin g) (Fin r) T := LinearMap.toMatrix'
    (φ ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.piScalarRight k T T (Fin r)).symm.toLinearMap) with hXdef
  -- the matrix presentation IS `φ`

    rw [hpt, congrAmbient_toSubmodule, divFamWindowGr_toSubmodule,

`divSchemeι`.  The kill law is `divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` at the chart ring itself
(spelled `Ideal.mk_ker`). -/
noncomputable def divCarveChartToDivScheme
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j))
      ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The defining triangle of the `DivScheme` chart atlas**: through the closed immersion
`divSchemeι`, the chart map of `Spec R_Z` is `Spec` of the quotient presentation
`divCarveChartMk` followed by the pair chart. -/
theorem divCarveChartToDivScheme_divSchemeι
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j).toRingHom)
        ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The atlas factorization of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3,
the DDR-9.F1 keystone): every test morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver` factors,
over a finite spanning family of basic localizations of `S`, through some chart
`divCarveChartToDivScheme i j` along a `k`-algebra map
`ω : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)` out of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring. -/
theorem divScheme_exists_chartFactor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ t : Fin m, ∃ (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
        (ω : DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ω.toRingHom)
            ≫ divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t))))
            ≫ v.left :=
  carveScheme_exists_chartFactor k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) S v

side component of every element of `K` lies in the span of the germ of the equation. -/
theorem germ_relThetaResSide_mem_span [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
    (z : relCurve C R) {ψ : relThetaSections C R π a} (hψ : ψ ∈ K)
    {y : relCurve C R} (hy : y ∈ D.piece z) :

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZariskiSep
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZariskiGlueKit
9	
10	/-!
11	# Locally certified divisor families: the `DivFamZar` carrier (DD-2 stage S5b)
12	
13	The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
14	Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
15	divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries
16	no global certificate — so the faithful functor value is the **locally certified**
17	quotient `DivFamZar`. The generic germ-regularity engines live in
18	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit`.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified` — the Addendum-2 frozen pin: a span-⊤ family
21	  `g : Fin m → R` with certified divisor families over `Localization.Away (g i)`
22	  divisor-equal to the pulled system; `hreg` is discharged by the Kit's open-immersion
23	  lemma, with the S4 instance provided by `haveI`.
24	* `IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq` — the pin respects divisor equality.
25	* `CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified` — a global certificate is a local one
26	  (trivial cover `g = ![1]`; the certified part is `mapAlg` to `Localization.Away 1`,
27	  whose equations ARE the pulled system on the nose).
28	* `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the mapAlg-hreg
29	  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
30	  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ
31	  sits over a chart `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` of `R'`, where the
32	  local certificate's regularity transports through its `DivEq` and the landed
33	  certificate-based pullback regularity.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar` — the quotient of locally certified systems by
35	  `DivEq`, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `picClass`, and `DivFam.toZar`.
36	
37	Total `DivFamZar.mapAlg` and the Zariski keystones are
38	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg` / `…ZarGlue`.
39	-/

42	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling

52	open Opposite

59	
60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
61	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
62	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]
63	
64	/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
65	local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
66	some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
67	localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
68	The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
69	open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
70	(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
71	def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
72	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
73	    ∀ i : Fin m,
74	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
75	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
76	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
77	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
78	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
79	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
80	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

82	variable {C R π}

85	transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
86	theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
87	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
88	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
89	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
90	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i

95	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
96	      h _ _)⟩

98	/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
99	certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
100	equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
101	the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
102	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
103	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
104	  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
105	  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
106	    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
107	  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
108	      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
109	    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
110	      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

117	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
118	
119	/-- **The mapAlg-hreg engine** (S5b): a locally certified system has regular pulled

127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical

134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions

149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩

222	`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
223	certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
226	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
227	  iseqv :=
228	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,

232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
233	degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
234	a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
235	def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)

242	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
243	    DivFamZar C R π n :=
244	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩

246	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
247	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
248	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=

255	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>

/-! ## `Spec` of an identity algebra map -/

/-- `Spec` of the identity `k`-algebra map is the identity morphism.

Stated for an abstract algebra `A` on purpose.  At `A := DivCarveChartRing …` the same
step inside a tactic block does not elaborate: the rewrite pattern of
`AlgHom.id_toRingHom` is stated through the `RingHom` coercion, and matching it against
the chart ring's `Ideal.Quotient` type forces the elaborator to unfold the quotient while
`glueData`'s `ULift` index is still being unified (recorded hazard).  Abstracting the
algebra keeps the rewrite at the level where the named lemmas apply. -/
theorem specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom)
      = CategoryStruct.id (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by
  have hid : (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom = RingHom.id A := rfl
  rw [hid, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]

/-! ## The clause is the classifier equation -/

include hO hchi in
/-- **`IsDivRepClassify` is an equation, not a property.**  The backward classifier
`divRepClassifyZar` is defined for every locally certified class over every affine test,
and `isDivRepClassify_unique` makes it the *unique* morphism satisfying the characterizing
clause.  So a morphism satisfies the clause for `F₀` exactly when it **is** the classifier
of `F₀`.

Forward is uniqueness against `divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify`; backward is a rewrite.
Mentioning no chart family and no universal point, this is what turns the DDR9-U
ε-identity into an equation between two already-existing morphisms of schemes (see
`DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq`). -/
theorem isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] (F₀ : DivFamZar C S pi g)
    (v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)) :
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀ v ↔
      (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F₀).left = v := by
  refine ⟨fun hv => ?_, fun hv => ?_⟩
  · exact isDivRepClassify_unique hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀
      (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀) hv
  · rw [← hv]
    exact divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀

/-! ## U2 as a per-chart equation of morphisms -/

namespace DivRepChartFamily

set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- Both directions instantiate `IsDivRepClassify` at the chart ring, whose `DivCarveChartRing`
-- quotient type the elaborator unfolds while unifying `divRepPullAt`'s `mapAlgHom`; the same
-- defeq profile as `IsChartClause.of_id`, which is budgeted identically.
include hO hchi in
/-- **U2, as an equation between morphisms** — and an **iff**, so it is a reduction of the
obligation rather than a restatement of it (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).

`IsChartClause U` holds exactly when, for each pair chart `(i, j)`, the backward
classifier of the supplied chart class *is* that chart's own map to `DivScheme`.  The
`ω`-quantifier collapses by `IsChartClause.of_id`, and the clause at the identity point is
the classifier equation by `isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq`.

So the DDR9-U ε-identity carries no residual quantifier over tower tests or framings: what
a producer owes is that two morphisms `Spec R_Z(i,j) ⟶ DivScheme g`, both of which already
exist unconditionally, agree. -/
theorem isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) :
    IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U ↔
      ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) (U i j)).left
          = ChartMap i j := by
  refine ⟨fun hU i j => ?_, fun hU => IsChartClause.of_id hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 fun i j => ?_⟩
  · -- instantiate the clause at the identity point of the chart
    have h := hU (S := ChartRing i j) i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
    rw [divRepPullAt_id] at h
    -- `Spec` of the identity algebra map is the identity; the rewrite is done at an
    -- ABSTRACT algebra (`specMap_ofHom_algHom_id`) because the same step spelled inline
    -- against the chart ring's quotient type does not elaborate.
    rw [specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (k := k), Category.id_comp] at h
    exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mp h
  · exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mpr (hU i j)

end DivRepChartFamily

/-- **Divisor representability from range membership of the chart maps** — the form this
file exists to state.

`divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`), so representability
of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to the classifier being surjective at every affine test.
This says surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices: if each chart map
`ChartMap i j` is the classifier of *some* locally certified class over its own chart ring
`R_Z(i,j)`, then `divFunctor C π g` is represented by `divSchemeOver`.

Nothing here produces such a class; per roadmap `…divrep.u2` that is the G-4 obligation.
The value is the shape of what is owed: a *preimage under a landed map*, at
`glueData`-many points, rather than a quantified submodule identity. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange
    (hrange : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),

      (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose)).mpr (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose_spec))

64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]

127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
131	  cases d; cases e
132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
133	  rfl

135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]

107	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor on `X`, adapted to a pointed cover:

109	is a nonzerodivisor (`regular`) and whose overlap ratios `eqn x / eqn y` are units
110	(`ratio_isUnit`). The class of the associated Čech cocycle of transition units is the
111	divisor class `𝒪(D)`, see `LocalEquations.picClass`. -/
112	structure LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
113	  /-- The pointed cover on whose members the local equations live. -/
114	  cover : X.PointedCover

117	  /-- Each local equation is regular: its germ at every point of its member is a
